faq.title: Work Agent questions for creators
faq.description: Practical answers about voice, sources, rights, channel fit, and what the creator must approve.

items.question: Is Floatboat a writing app or social scheduler?
items.answer: Floatboat is a Work Agent for content assignments, not a writing app or scheduler. It uses a persistent workspace to organize approved inputs, drafts, adaptations, and review steps while you continue using your preferred editor and publishing tools.

items.question: Will every channel version sound the same?
items.answer: It should not. Define the audience, format, length, voice, and purpose for each channel, then review each result against the approved source rather than requesting generic repurposing.

items.question: Can it learn from my existing work?
items.answer: You can provide selected examples and a style guide, but the creator should still review whether a draft reflects the intended voice instead of treating imitation as guaranteed.

items.question: How do I prevent invented facts or citations?
items.answer: Keep research tied to inspectable sources, distinguish source notes from original commentary, and verify every factual claim before publication.

items.question: What about copyrighted or licensed source material?
items.answer: Use only material you are allowed to process and adapt. Permissions, attribution, licensing, and fair-use decisions remain with the creator.

items.question: Will Floatboat publish automatically?
items.answer: The recommended workflow ends with a release package for review. Account access, publication, and irreversible channel actions should remain explicitly approved.

items.question: What is a good first creator workflow?
items.answer: Choose one finished long-form piece and adapt it into two clearly different channels. Judge fidelity and usefulness before saving the process.

finalCta.title: Keep the original voice across the release package
finalCta.description: Start from the approved draft or recording. Prepare captions and channel versions, then review tone and claims before publishing.
